angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 325,866 km at 43.85 pc = 0.1 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 22.8048 +/- 0.0199 mas (same row, RUWE 1.25): 43.85 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.4684 +/- 0.0087 solar radii from Distler et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-4364 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169..166D/abstract): 325,866 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.487 +/- 0.017 solar masses from Distler et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-4364 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169..166D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3528 +/- 33 K from Distler et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4364 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169..166D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Distler et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4364 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169..166D/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-4364.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.784, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
